text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Moslem chairman of Bosnia's collective presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, urges the Council of Ministers to adopt a package of economic reform laws or an international donors' conference set for mid-April will be postponed again.
- Bosnia's federation political parties believe that an attempt to divide Bosnia along religious lines would cause damage mostly to Bosnian Moslems.
- Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic denies recent speculation in Sarajevo media that Moslem leadership is preparing for a tacit division of the country.
- A group of Bosnian refugees who resettled in Germany in 1992 will be returned to Bosnia on Tuesday. Most of them are refugees from Serb-held areas in Bosnia.
- Moslem co-chairman of Bosnia's central cabinet, Haris Silajdzic, said at Islamic conference in Islamabad that Islam as a set of rules could help the world's positive development.
- Moslem chairman of Bosnia's three-man presidency Alija Izetbegovic is due to meet U.S. president Bill Clinton on Wednesday in Washington.

- Michael Steiner, deputy to international High Representative to Bosnia, condemns Croat authorities over handling of trial of five Croat policemen in the divided town of Mostar who were accused of opening fire on a crowd of Moslems. Three policemen received suspended sentences and two were acquitted.

- Moslem-Croat Federation government Prime Minister Bicakcic met Fransican clergyman to discuss recent attacks on Roman Catholic churches in central Bosnia and security preparations for scheduled visit of Pope John Paul II. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
